title: Probabilistic calibration orchestrator and golden-suite validator for quant profiles
creator: Aisha Martin
description:
Goal: Build an automated accuracy validation harness that validates FP8/INT8 quantization profiles against a curated golden-prompt suite and probabilistic calibration workflows. The harness must produce deterministic pass/fail gates, surface regression signals early, and integrate with CI, Canary rollouts, and the Console dashboards.

Problems we're solving:
- Calibration drift: when a model's quantization calibration set no longer represents production distributions.
- Subtle semantic regressions introduced by FP8/INT8 quant transforms that are not captured by simple token-level metrics.
- Flaky thresholds: tests that pass locally but fail in the CI due to sampling variability.

Core features and requirements:
1) Golden prompt suite: curated across domains (conversational, code, summarization, QA, retrieval-augmented prompts). Each prompt should include: seed, ordering, expected reference outputs (multiple acceptable variants), and grading hints. Prompts are versioned and stored in an S3-backed catalog.

2) Metric set: multi-tier metrics including exact-match / F1 for QA, ROUGE-L, BLEU (where relevant), semantic similarity (embedding cosine + BERTScore as tie-breaker), log-prob delta distributions, token-level perplexity change, and downstream acceptance heuristics (e.g., compile/run tests for code). For each metric we will define: direction (higher/lower better), aggregation (median/95p), and regression sensitivity.

3) Probabilistic calibration workflow: run multiple seeds / temperature samples for non-deterministic decoders; compute distributional deltas vs baseline (float32) and derive p-values and effect sizes. Automatically propose dynamic thresholds using bootstrap confidence intervals rather than fixed single-number thresholds.

4) Pass/fail gates: hierarchical gating: critical gates (blocking releases) and advisory gates (alert only). Critical gates include high-severity QA EM drop > 2% absolute on production-critical prompts, and BERTScore semantic drop beyond calibrated CI. Advisory gates include minor ROUGE shifts or increases in tail latency of scoring.

5) Flakiness mitigation: use repeated runs, seed stabilization, and Bayesian posterior estimates to reduce false positives. If a test toggles between pass/fail across 3 runs, mark it flaky and file an auto-ticket.

6) CI and Canary integration: harness should run on PRs that touch quant pipelines + nightly full-run. Canary policy: if a release candidate fails critical gates on canary subset, automatically block rollout and create an incident runbook link.

7) Observability & dashboarding: surface per-prompt metrics, drift timelines, top failing prompts, calibration histograms, and golden-suite health on Console. Add ability to view raw model tokens and log-prob traces for failed examples.

8) Automation and remediation: when a quant profile fails, the harness should automatically attempt a quick re-calibration (re-run calibration with expanded seed set or alternative calibration optimizer) and re-evaluate; if re-calibration recovers quality, mark as "auto-repaired" with a human-in-the-loop approval step.

Design constraints and non-goals:
- Non-goal: fully replacing human QA for semantic-edge cases. The harness should reduce noise and flag high-confidence regressions; final triage may be manual.
- Non-goal: exhaustive test coverage for every user corpus in first iteration. We'll focus on high-impact production prompts and a stratified random sample of customers.

Implementation outline and milestones:
M1 (Week 1-2): scaffold harness interface + golden prompt catalog schema + S3 storage + lightweight runner that compares float32 vs quantized model for token-level diffs.
M2 (Week 3-4): implement metric plugins (EM/F1, BERTScore, log-prob delta) and bootstrap threshold library. Add seed sampling harness for non-deterministic metrics.
M3 (Week 5): CI integration + nightly job + flaky-detection. Add auto-ticketing for flaky tests.
M4 (Week 6-7): remediation flow (auto re-calibration), canary hook, and Console dashboard panels.
M5 (Week 8): end-to-end tests, load testing for harness scale, and runbook for blocked rollouts.

Acceptance criteria:
- The harness can run the golden suite end-to-end against a provided FP8 and INT8 profile and produce a reproducible report (JSON + human-readable summary).
- Critical gates trigger a blocking signal in CI when thresholds are exceeded and create a ticket with context and top failing prompts.
- Flaky detection reduces CI false positives by >= 60% vs current single-run checks (measure via baseline historical runs).
- Console dashboard surfaces per-prompt time-series and top regressions; links to raw artifacts (diffs, log-probs, seeds).
- Auto-recalibration flow recovers at least 50% of transient calibration failures in a controlled A/B test.

Risks and mitigation:
- Risk: thresholds too sensitive -> noisy blocking. Mitigation: bootstrap CIs and beta-stage advisory gates before enabling critical gate in CI.
- Risk: expensive to run at scale -> limit to canary / stratified samples; parallelize using batch-runner and sampling heuristics.
- Risk: complex metrics slow down CI -> run heavy metrics in nightly/full jobs and fast heuristics in PR-run.
